source.citation: Kulik, D. A. (2011). Improving the structural consistency of C-S-H solid solution thermodynamic models. Cement and Concrete Research 41, 477-495.

transcription.from: the published article (PDF), Section 4.2 and Tables 2 and 3 read on the rendered page
transcription.note: The ternary CSH3T model of tobermorite-like C-S-H: two bridging-tetrahedral sites BTI1 and BTI2, each holding one Si0.5OH+ or one HO0.5Ca0.5+ species (abbreviated Si and Ca here), with coefficient 1 in the sublattice formula of Eq. (17), per formula unit of Table 2 (3 tetrahedral sites). Eq. (19) gives the activity of each end-member as the product of its two site fractions; the model is ideal. Table 2 writes the sublattice formula of T5C with its Si species first, [Si0.5OH+]1:[HO0.5Ca0.5+]1, while Eq. (19) puts its Ca on BTI1 and its Si on BTI2. The two readings differ only by the names given to the two sites, which changes no activity; the occupancy transcribed here follows Eq. (19).

csh3t_end_members.location: Table 3, bulk formulas (Table 2 prints the same compositions factored)

notes: csh3t_site_mixing_terms is Eq. (19) transcribed on its own, independently of csh3t_occupancy: each row is one term coefficient x ln(sum of the listed mole fractions) of the logarithm of the activity of the end-member the equation is written for. The test suite requires the two transcriptions to give the same activities.

The end-members of the Cemdata18 file (CSH3T-TobH, CSH3T-T5C, CSH3T-T2C) are half the formula units of Table 3. The site coefficients of a model built on them are therefore halved, which sublattice_model does from the formulas.
The species formulas are given without their charge (+1 each); the vacancy site VCH and the shared sites carry no species that varies between end-members.
Section 4.2 also gives a variant with the two BTI sites doubled (Eqs. (22)-(24)); it is not transcribed here.
